summary: Round-2 results review passes. The eight full 100k cases and four pilots in job 44033881 (COMPLETED 0:0, 43m03s, sdfampere038) are complete, internally consistent, and faithfully summarized by results.json/validation.json/README.md. Checked directly against the SHA-indexed native snapshots under build/bd-review-evidence: each full case row set shows exactly 500,000 requests == completions and 335,820,000,000 bytes with per-BD histograms {524724:k, 629664:k, 734604:3k}; bd_events sum to 100,000 in every case (e.g. 25800+24200+24700+25300); 1,000 callbacks per full case each of size 100 with two distinct CUDA stream pointers alternating per BD; pressure_drains and cpu_reads 0; drain rows closed/pending 0/active 0/held 0/peers == bds; all five staged files 0 resident pages in conditioning and initial_cache for every case; nic_delta rx_bytes reproduce every README value (332.376–341.767 GiB, 1.063–1.093x payload, second port 0) and envelope excess 1.513–1.753 s; idle RX 0.96–1.03 MiB/s. Rates recompute (e.g. 312.7567 GiB / 69.3746 s = 4.5082 GiB/s), medians/speedups (3.7866x) and the 29.4% 4-vs-3 BD gain are correct. Framework settings in all 12 case files are batch 100 / streams 2 / 6 GiB / 524288 / SMD 1000; device dicts show the single masked UUID GPU-275eeecd..., compat ON, 8 threads, 1 MiB tasks, 16 MiB bounce, auto-direct off; runtime_files hashes are identical across ranks and match the eight frozen module copies in copy-index and the five common hashes in baseline-runtime-comparison.json (previous-baseline.json records only those five). The frozen gpu_events.py/gpu_kvikio_read.py confirm every read goes through KvikioGpuReader._submit_read/wait_batch (the bulk group path at gpu_events.py:813-840 and _wait_gpu_read both use the reader), _trim_gpu_caches is only invoked on GpuMemoryPressureError, and n_gpu_streams drives the pool depth, so the accounting and stream checks are meaningful. audit.py has 22 distinct fail-closed checks and test_audit.py's 22 tests (1 positive + 21 mutations) each target a distinct message, matching tests.log 'Ran 22 tests ... OK'. Cleanup receipt shows the unique FFB stage removed; artifact-index and copy-index SHAs agree (31 native + baseline + 8 runtime = 40). BDS-01/03/04/05 are resolved as claimed; BDS-02 remains deferred and documented. New non-blocking items: BDS-06 (README omits that the prior accepted one-BD one-stream rate was ~2.19 GiB/s on sdfampere042 versus 1.19 GiB/s here, so the 3.79x headline rests on a one-BD baseline ~45% below the prior campaign), BDS-07 (per-BD outstanding peak equals exactly one subbatch, i.e. no two read batches overlapped within a BD, worth stating as an interpretation aid), BDS-08 (tests.log has no command/source path). No framework code changed; acceptance evidence is complete.

limitations: No commands executed: SHA-256 digests in copy-index/artifact-index, the audit run, and the 22-test run were not reproduced by this reviewer; test results are taken from tests.log and the coordinator statement. tests.log does not record the command or source directory used.

Long arrays (timestamps, callbacks) in the 6 MB case files were inspected selectively via grep and head reads, not exhaustively; exact global partition and ordering are relied on from audit.py's fail-closed checks.

Only eight frozen runtime modules were copied; psana.psexp.event_manager (the patched _read hook), gpu_input_group.py, gpu_group_schedule internals and mpi_ds.py were not inspected in frozen form. Routing of all reads through _submit_read is inferred from exact request/byte counts plus the inspected gpu_events.py call sites.
inputs.json (2.4 MB) could not be read in full due to tool size limits; only the header and first timestamps were read.
Cold-cache claims cover Linux page cache (mincore) only; Weka client/backend and SMD caches are uncontrolled as the README states, and NIC byte ratios cannot yield an exact cache-hit fraction.
No GPU timeline or utilization data exists, so stream overlap and the cause of near-linear BD scaling remain unattributed, as the README discloses.

findings.evidence: The README states node, stream count and dataset length differ from the historical one-BD measurement but never gives the prior rate. previous-baseline.json (sdfampere042, 1 BD, 1 stream, 10k events, cold) recorded 2.1884 GiB/s (its repeat 2.1197) while this sweep's 1-BD two-stream 100k cases are 1.174-1.204 GiB/s. The '3.79 x the one-BD rate' headline is therefore relative to a one-BD baseline roughly 45% below the previously accepted one-BD result; 4 BDs at 4.50 GiB/s is about 2.06x that earlier single-BD rate.
findings.requested_change: State the prior accepted one-BD rate (2.19/2.12 GiB/s, one stream, 10k, sdfampere042) next to the current 1-BD rate in the README and results.json notes, and say explicitly that the two-stream single-BD configuration on this node ran slower than the earlier one-stream result, so the 3.79x speedup is relative to this sweep's own baseline only. Wording/disclosure only; no rerun required.

findings.evidence: peak_outstanding_requests is exactly 500 and peak_outstanding_bytes exactly 335,820,000 for every BD in every case, which equals one 100-event subbatch (5 reads x 100 events). bulk_accounting.py sums all pending batches at issue time, so a peak of one subbatch means no two read batches were ever in flight simultaneously within a BD; I/O for subbatch k+1 is issued only after subbatch k's wait completes (gpu_events.py:1059-1072). The README calls these 'queue bookkeeping peaks' but does not state this implication.
findings.requested_change: Optional: add one sentence that the per-BD peak equals exactly one subbatch, so storage reads within a BD were serialized at subbatch granularity and multi-BD scaling adds I/O concurrency across processes rather than within one. Interpretation aid only.

findings.evidence: tests.log contains only the unittest dots, 'Ran 22 tests in 5.241s' and 'OK'; it does not record the interpreter, audit/test command or the source directory passed as SOURCE to test_audit.py, unlike the prior campaign README which listed the validation commands.
findings.requested_change: Optional: add the exact audit.py and test_audit.py commands (with the native artifact root) to the README or tests.log so the recorded result is reproducible without the coordinator statement.
